column1: Hardware|Which component executes instructions in a computer?|CPU|Monitor|Printer|Keyboard|The CPU fetches, decodes and executes instructions; peripherals handle input or output.

Hardware|Which memory usually loses its contents when power is removed?|RAM|ROM|Optical disc|Flash drive|RAM is volatile working memory. Persistent storage retains data without normal operating power.
Hardware|Which device is primarily an input device?|Scanner|Projector|Speaker|Printer|A scanner converts physical documents or images into digital input.
Hardware|Which device is primarily an output device?|Monitor|Mouse|Microphone|Keyboard|A monitor presents processed information to the user.
Hardware|What is the basic unit of binary information?|Bit|Byte|Kilobyte|Gigabyte|A bit has two possible values, conventionally written as 0 and 1.
Hardware|How many bits make one byte?|8|2|4|16|A byte contains eight bits in the standard convention used by modern computers.
Hardware|What is the decimal value of binary 1010?|10|8|11|12|Read place values from right to left: 0×1 + 1×2 + 0×4 + 1×8 = 10.

Hardware|Why is cache memory useful?|It reduces access time for frequently used data|It replaces all permanent storage|It converts text into images|It increases monitor size|Cache keeps frequently needed data close to the processor, reducing slower memory accesses.

Hardware|Which storage device normally has no moving mechanical parts?|SSD|Magnetic hard disk|Optical disc drive|Floppy drive|An SSD uses electronic memory rather than rotating platters and a moving read/write head.

Hardware|What is an operating system mainly responsible for?|Managing hardware resources and application execution|Only designing slides|Only printing photographs|Only calculating tax|An operating system coordinates processes, memory, files and access to devices.
Files|Which filename extension commonly denotes a PDF document?|.pdf|.xlsx|.mp3|.jpg|PDF is a document format; the other extensions commonly identify a spreadsheet, audio or image.

Files|What does a folder provide in a file system?|A way to organize files and subfolders|A guarantee against malware|An extra CPU core|A faster network connection|Folders organize file paths; they do not by themselves improve security or hardware performance.

Files|What is the main purpose of a backup?|Keeping a recoverable copy of important data|Deleting the original automatically|Sharing every file publicly|Increasing screen resolution|A backup supports recovery after loss or damage. It should be checked and stored separately where appropriate.
Files|Which action changes a file's location rather than making another copy?|Move|Copy|Preview|Print|Moving places the file at another path; copying leaves a second instance.

Word processing|What is mail merge used for?|Creating personalized documents from one template and a data source|Combining several operating systems|Removing every duplicate word|Encrypting a hard drive|Mail merge inserts fields such as a recipient name into a common letter or label template.

Word processing|What does a header usually contain?|Content repeated at the top of pages|Only the last word in a document|Every footnote's body|A spreadsheet formula|Headers commonly hold repeated titles or identifiers. Section settings can change which pages share a header.

Word processing|Which alignment distributes text between both left and right margins?|Justified|Left aligned|Centered|Right aligned|Justified paragraphs adjust spacing to align most lines with both margins.

Word processing|Why are heading styles useful?|They give documents structure and support automatic tables of contents|They force every page into landscape|They delete all paragraph spacing|They protect documents from all viruses|Semantic heading styles support consistent formatting, navigation and generated contents.

Word processing|What is the purpose of Find and Replace?|Locating specified text and optionally substituting another text|Repairing a broken screen|Changing the processor|Converting RAM to ROM|Find identifies matching text. Replace can change those matches; review scope before using Replace All.

Word processing|What does Track Changes help reviewers see?|Recorded edits to document content|All websites visited by the author|The computer's temperature|Every printed document in the office|Tracked edits make proposed insertions and deletions visible for review and acceptance or rejection.
Spreadsheets|What identifies a cell at column B and row 7?|B7|7B|BB|R7|In A1 notation, the column letter precedes the row number.
Spreadsheets|Which formula adds cells A1 through A5?|=SUM(A1:A5)|=COUNT(A1:A5)|=MAX(A1:A5)|=MIN(A1:A5)|SUM adds numeric values in the selected range; COUNT counts numeric entries.
Spreadsheets|What does =AVERAGE(2,4,6) return?|4|3|6|12|The arithmetic mean is the total 12 divided by the three values.
Spreadsheets|Which reference locks both column and row when copied?|$B$3|B3|$B3|B$3|A dollar sign before both coordinates makes both parts absolute.
Spreadsheets|Which reference locks the row but lets the column change?|B$3|$B3|B3|$B$3|B$3 is mixed: row 3 stays fixed while the column can adjust.
Spreadsheets|What does =IF(5>3,"Yes","No") return?|Yes|No|5|3|IF evaluates the condition, returning its second argument when true and its third when false.

Spreadsheets|What does COUNT usually count in a range?|Cells containing numeric values|All blank cells|Only formatting styles|Only worksheet names|COUNT counts numbers. COUNTA counts non-empty cells and COUNTBLANK counts blank cells.
Spreadsheets|Which function selects the largest numeric value in a range?|MAX|MIN|LEFT|LOWER|MAX returns the greatest numeric value; MIN returns the least.

Spreadsheets|Why can a chart be misleading if its axis is truncated?|It can exaggerate apparent differences|It removes all numerical data|It makes every category equal|It changes the actual source values|An altered axis scale changes visual comparisons; inspect labels and units before interpreting.

Presentations|What does a slide master help manage?|Common slide layout and formatting|Only the computer's sound card|Only spreadsheet arithmetic|Only browser bookmarks|A slide master provides shared design elements and layout settings across slides.

Presentations|How does a transition differ from an animation?|A transition controls movement between slides|A transition changes only file permissions|An animation always affects all slides|Both always encrypt the file|Transitions act between slides; animations affect objects or content within a slide.
Networking|What does LAN stand for?|Local Area Network|Large Arithmetic Number|Linear Address Note|Long Access Node|A LAN connects devices within a limited geographic area, such as a building.

Networking|What does DNS primarily do?|Resolve domain names to network addresses|Calculate spreadsheet averages|Store only video frames|Print web pages automatically|DNS helps clients locate hosts using domain names rather than requiring users to memorize numeric addresses.

Networking|Which protocol is associated with encrypted web connections?|HTTPS|Plain HTTP|Unencrypted FTP|Telnet|HTTPS carries HTTP over an encrypted connection; encryption does not prove the site's honesty.
Networking|How long is an IPv4 address?|32 bits|8 bits|64 bits|128 bits|IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses. IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses.
Networking|How long is an IPv6 address?|128 bits|16 bits|32 bits|48 bits|IPv6 provides a larger address space using 128-bit addresses.

Networking|What is a router mainly used for?|Forwarding packets between networks|Only typing documents|Only changing font size|Only scanning images|Routers choose paths and forward traffic between connected networks.

Networking|What does a URL identify?|The address of a resource|A CPU instruction register|A printer ink colour|A spreadsheet total|A URL specifies how and where a resource can be accessed, often using a scheme, host and path.
Networking|Which email field hides recipients from other recipients?|BCC|CC|Subject|To|Blind carbon copy recipients are not displayed in the ordinary recipient list to others.
Networking|Which protocol is mainly associated with sending email?|SMTP|IMAP|POP3|DNS|SMTP handles email submission and transfer; IMAP and POP3 are used for retrieval.
Networking|Which protocol supports keeping email folders synchronized with a server?|IMAP|SMTP|ARP|FTP|IMAP supports server-based mailbox access and synchronization across clients.

Security|What is phishing?|Deceptive messages that try to obtain information or provoke unsafe actions|A guaranteed secure backup method|A type of monitor|An automatic grammar check|Phishing impersonates trusted parties. Check the sender, destination and requested action independently.

Security|What distinguishes ransomware?|It blocks access to data or systems and demands payment|It always improves system speed|It only changes display brightness|It is a spreadsheet function|Ransomware commonly encrypts files or otherwise prevents access. Backups and updates reduce recovery risk.

Security|What is a firewall primarily designed to do?|Filter network traffic according to rules|Make every password public|Increase paper size|Automatically verify all facts|A firewall permits or blocks traffic using configured rules; it is one part of security.

Security|Why is multi-factor authentication useful?|It requires more than one type of authentication evidence|It removes the need for account recovery|It guarantees phishing can never occur|It shares passwords with everyone|Combining independent factors makes a stolen password alone less useful to an attacker.

Security|Which practice is best for different online accounts?|Use unique strong passwords|Reuse one short password everywhere|Send passwords in public posts|Store passwords in a shared document without controls|Unique passwords limit the damage when one account's credentials are compromised.

Security|What is the principle of least privilege?|Grant only the access needed for a task|Give every user administrator access|Disable all auditing|Make every file public|Least privilege reduces unnecessary access and limits the impact of mistakes or compromised accounts.

Security|Why should software updates be installed from trusted sources?|They may fix known vulnerabilities and bugs|They always double hardware capacity|They make backups unnecessary|They allow passwords to be removed|Trusted updates can address security defects. Read material compatibility changes before applying them.

Security|Which action is safest for an unexpected attachment?|Verify its source and purpose before opening|Enable every macro immediately|Forward it to all contacts|Disable security scanning|Unexpected files can contain malicious code. Independent verification is safer than trusting appearance alone.

Accessibility|What does alternative text for an informative image provide?|A textual description for people who cannot see the image|A substitute for every caption in every context|A password for the image|A larger file size guarantee|Alt text communicates the image's purpose or information to assistive technology users.
